highlights:
# An interesting observation: Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates on Oct 1. H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 … | Chris Li · LinkedIn · 2026-10-13T00:00:00+00:00

**Chris Li**: LLM Inference will become the largest fungible commodity.

---

An interesting observation: Nebius raised on-demand GPU rates on Oct 1. H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
Meanwhile, Anthropic launched Claude Haiku 5.5 on Oct 7 at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens, for prompts up to 100K. Haiku 4.5 was $1 and $5. The arithmetic, counting output tokens only: $4.50 / $0.50 per million = 9M output tokens to pay for one H100-hour, or 2,500 tokens a second for the whole hour. At the old $3.85 rent and Haiku 4.5s $5 price: 770K tokens, about 214 a second.

Real serving is messier. Input tokens also earn, and a small model with good batching can clear 2,500 a second on one card. A model that needs the whole card for one replica has a harder time. Haiku is a closed model Anthropic serves itself, so nobody rents an H100 to run it. But this is the price open-model hosts get measured against now.

highlights:
### Nebius: preemptible rates and EU options

Nebius quotes an H100 at $3.85 per GPU-hour on-demand, with a $4.50 rate effective October 1, 2026, an H200 at $4.50, and an HGX B200 at $7.15. Its preemptible tier is where the price drops: H100 and H200 from $0.79 per GPU-hour, and B200 from $0.99. It is not aimed at hobbyists; the catalog leans toward data-center cards rather than laptop-class 24GB GPUs.

...

- Vast.ai rates are medians, not list prices. Its feed states that prices update hourly and reflect currently available offers, so the $1.60/hr H100 is a market median, not a rate guaranteed for your job. Its cheapest tier is interruptible and can be reclaimed.
- CoreWeave has no single-GPU tier. You buy an 8-GPU node, so a solo developer pays for eight cards even when the job needs one.
- Nebius prices step up. The H100 rate moves to $4.50 per GPU-hour effective October 1, 2026, and the B200 to $8.50.
- Lambda adds tax. Its listed rates are plus applicable sales tax, VAT, or GST, and self-serve capacity is first-come rather than reserved.
- RunPod's two tiers differ on more than price. Community Cloud is peer-hosted and cheaper; Secure Cloud is data-center hosted and costs more per hour for the same card.
- Vast.ai's data carries a license note. Its pricing feed is free to cite with attribution, but bulk collection or redistribution requires a data license from the company.

results.title: 🚀 The NeoCloud Explosion: Why AI Teams Are Ditching Hyperscalers in 2026 | AntGPU
highlights:
💰 The "Hyperscaler Premium" Tax
On-demand access to NVIDIA H100s at major cloud providers remains priced around $7.89 to $12.29/hr, whereas specialized NeoClouds offer identical compute performance for $3.49 to $5.33/hr.
That is a 48% to 80% price gap for raw AI compute power.

💡 Why the Gap Keeps Widening
Focused Infrastructure: Bare-metal deployments optimized specifically for Slurm, Kubernetes, and InfiniBand clusters without legacy hypervisor overhead.
Generational Upgrades: Rapid rollout of Blackwell architectures (B200, B300, GB300) that increase density and lower per-token inference costs.
Capacity Availability: Direct allocation of hardware to dedicated LLM workloads rather than shared multi-tenant cloud partitions.
By the end of this year, industry estimates project specialized AI clouds will handle over 80% of independent AI training and inference workloads.

results.title: 【数据显微镜】再涨20％：GPU租金二度上调，算力缺口仍在拉大 - OFweek智能硬件网
highlights:
9月中旬，云计算服务提供商Nebius向客户发出调价通知，拟自10月1日起上调主要英伟达GPU的按需(on-demand)租金：H100由每小时3.85美元升至4.50美元，H200由4.50美元升至5.40美元，B200由7.15美元升至8.50美元，B300由7.85美元升至9.50美元，本轮涨幅约17%至21%。

这已是该公司年内第二次全面上调按需价格。若按两轮公开报价计算，以其首轮调价前的6.10美元为起点，B300每小时租金年内累计涨幅已达约56%。

价格连续上行的另一面，是算力供需缺口仍在拉大。中国信通院数据显示，2026年一季度，国内AI算力需求同比增长417%，同期有效供给增速仅为128%。从海外按需报价到国内合同金额，价格上行的链条正被逐段验证。

01. 一条两度抬升的价格曲线

本轮调价并非孤立事件。今年5月宣布、6月1日生效的一轮提价中，Nebius已将H100由2.95美元/小时升至3.85美元，H200由3.50美元升至4.50美元，B200由5.50美元升至7.15美元，B300由6.10美元升至7.85美元，整体涨幅约29%。

两轮叠加，Nebius自身报价序列的绝对水平因此被逐轮抬升。按需价格值得单独拿出来看，在于它是新签合同与中小客户最直接的定价锚：按需价上移，意味着边际零售价格体系同步抬升。

浙商证券认为，这轮上调是“长约、短约、按需”价格全线上移的确认。更能说明紧张程度的是，涨价范围已溢出加速卡本身。同批调整中，纯CPU计算的AMD EPYC Genoa由0.012美元/vCPU小时上调25%至0.015美元，Genoa内存由0.0032美元/GiB小时上调约41%至0.0045美元，供给偏紧不只发生在GPU一隅，而是覆盖了算力基础设施的多个环节。

...

如果说海外按需报价反映的是零售端的即时供需，那么国内上市公司的合同金额，则是价格上行进入报表的证据。9月16日晚间，赛意信息发布公告称，公司与客户就高性能算力服务合同签订补充协议，将其中一份合同含税金额由36亿元调整为38.7亿元，两份合同合并含税总金额由64.5亿元调整为67.2亿元，增加2.7亿元。

results.title: If you track GPU prices by checking vendor pages, last week would have looked like nothing happened. | Bobby Clay
highlights:
Across the nine providers we track, not one published on-demand price moved more than 1% between the October 4 and October 11 catalogs, and all four family floors held.

Every gap against the traded market moved anyway. On October 11 the lowest published H100 across those nine sat $1.25 above the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones. On October 4 it sat $1.31 above. The published price never moved. The index did.

AWS also put B300 into its EU (London) catalog on October 11, from $27.19 to $27.67 per GPU-hour, as five listings for one machine. Same hardware, same region, same day. What differs is the operating system.
A flat week on the pricing pages was not a flat week.

results.title: GPU rental prices continue to rise and the Blackwell chips are leading the way. On-demand prices for both NVIDIA’s B200 and B300 in the US have been climbing. The B300 is rising … | Annan Lu
highlights:
GPU rental prices continue to rise and the Blackwell chips are leading the way. On-demand prices for both NVIDIA’s B200 and B300 in the US have been climbing. The B300 is rising faster, and the gap between the two is growing.

From our latest discussions with compute buyers, we've found that these are the major reasons driving the delta:
1. 𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐲 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭. The B300’s 288 GB of HBM3e (vs. 192 GB on the B200) relies on 12-high memory stacks that are expensive and hard to manufacture. Fewer units are reaching the market.
2. 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐚 𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐤. B300 systems draw up to 1,400 W per GPU at rack scale and often need liquid cooling. Not every data center can host them.
3. 𝐃𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐦𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦 𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠. Long-context reasoning models and large MoE models have massive KV caches, and the B300’s 288 GB gives them roughly 50% more room than the B200’s 192 GB. That extra memory means bigger batches, longer contexts, and fewer GPUs per model replica, so teams running these workloads are choosing the B300 even at a premium.

Higher hourly price doesn’t mean a higher cost per token. If  extra memory lets you serve more users per GPU, the B300 can still come out cheaper.

results.title: FPT and Elice first read October 12, 2026: H100 SXM $2.99 and $3.57
highlights:
On October 12, 2026 we read two Asian GPU clouds for the first time: FPT AI Factory, the GPU cloud of the Vietnamese IT group FPT, and Elice Cloud, run by Elice of Seoul. In our read of 06:39 UTC on October 13 FPT listed a one-GPU H100 SXM virtual machine in Southeast Asia at $2.99 an hour and Elice a one-GPU H100 SXM instance at $3.57. The H100 SXM page printed a median rate card of $3.49 over 37 providers: FPT’s rate was ninth from the bottom and Elice’s 21st.

...

FPT’s pricing page is a static document with several service tabs; we read its GPU Virtual Machine tab, where each machine of one to eight GPUs comes with CPU, memory, storage and a public IP. Five cards are listed there for one GPU: the B300 at $6.99, the H100 SXM at $2.99, the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell at $2.19 and the A30 at $1.06, all captioned Southeast Asia, and the H200 at $6.60, captioned Japan. The page prints these in US dollars and says nothing about VAT.

Elice’s page draws its table with JavaScript, so we read it rendered. Each cell prints a discount, a struck-through list figure and the rate charged per hour; we read only the charged rate, for the one-GPU row. Those were $6.82 for the B200, $3.57 for the H100 SXM and $1.62 for the A100 80GB on demand, and $6.14, $3.21 and $1.46 for the same instances as spot. The spot gap is shown by subtraction: $3.57 - $3.21 = $0.36 on the H100, $6.82 - $6.14 = $0.68 on the B200, $1.62 - $1.46 = $0.16 on the A100. Reserved terms read “Contact sales”, so no committed rate is listed for either provider.

...

Our card pages take each provider’s cheapest on-demand rate as its rate card and print the median of those. In the build of 06:39 UTC on October 13, FPT’s B300 at $6.99 was fifth lowest of 22 rate cards, where the median was $8.69, and its H100 SXM ninth of 37 under the $3.49 median. Its RTX PRO 6000 at $2.19 sat 15th of 36, just under the median of $2.21. Its other two rates stood above their medians: the A30 at $1.06 was seventh of eight against $0.48, and the H200 in Japan at $6.60 was 41st of 49 against $4.54.

Elice’s B200 at $6.82 was 16th of 34 rate cards, under the B200 median of $6.99. Its H100 SXM at $3.57 stood above the $3.49 median and its A100 80GB at $1.62 was 22nd of 56, under that card’s median of $1.92. Neither provider was the cheapest on any of its cards in that read, by our per-provider check over the published prices.

All eleven rates are whole instances with CPU and memory, not the GPU alone, and each row on our pages carries that scope as a tag. Both providers list in US dollars, so their H100 SXM rates are constituents of the H100 Price Index for the week of October 12, still provisional at $3.49 over 35 quotes from 33 providers in that read. Nothing here is forecast: these are two price lists as we first read them.

results.title: GPU price index explained: list prices, marketplace medians and transaction indices — AI Compute Radar
highlights:
### Silicon Data

- Launched the Silicon Data H100 Rental Index (Bloomberg ticker SDH100RT) on 20 May 2025: a daily rate built from 3.5 million pricing data points across rental platforms.
- Standardises each observation for machine specification, rental terms and location, and publishes separate neocloud and hyperscaler readings.
- CME Group announced the Silicon Data H100 and B200 Rental Index Futures on 11 August 2026: listed on NYMEX, each contract a month's worth of rent for one GPU, planned for 5 October 2026 pending regulatory review.

Sources: Silicon Data press release, 20 May 2025 ↗ Silicon Data H100 index page, 13 October 2026 ↗ CME Group press release, 11 August 2026 ↗

### Ornn

- Publishes the Ornn Compute Price Index (OCPI), described by ICE as the first compute index built only from printed transactions, for H100, H200, B200, RTX 5090 and other GPUs.
- Ornn's B200 page describes each daily value as a volume-weighted, winsorised average of transacted rental prices, settled once per trading day at 4:00 p.m. New York time.
- Intercontinental Exchange announced cash-settled GPU compute futures on OCPI on 19 May 2026, to launch subject to regulatory approval.

Sources: ICE press release, 19 May 2026 ↗ Ornn B200 market page, 13 October 2026 ↗

...

- Kalshi lists yes-or-no contracts on rental prices for the A100, H100, H200, B200 and RTX 5090 that reference the Ornn Compute Price Index, as reported on 17 August 2026.

...

1. 01 Which GPU exactly?

An H100 SXM and an H100 PCIe are different machines; so are 80 GB and 94 GB versions. A price without the variant compares unlike things.
2. 02 Which term?

On-demand, spot, interruptible and reserved capacity are priced differently; a monthly commitment is not an hourly rate.
3. 03 Posted, offered or paid?

results.title: On CoreWeave's rate card, an H200 costs 2.4% more per GPU-hour than an H100: $6.31 against $6.16. | Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
On CoreWeave's rate card, an H200 costs 2.4% more per GPU-hour than an H100: $6.31 against $6.16.

The H200 has 141 GB of memory per GPU. The H100 has 80 GB. That's 76% more memory for a 2.4% price difference.

Both are sold as 8-GPU nodes, $50.44 an hour against $49.24, with the same 128 vCPUs and 2,048 GB of system RAM per node.

Per GB of GPU memory, that works out to about $0.045 an hour on the H200 and $0.077 on the H100. For workloads limited by memory, such as long contexts and large KV caches, that's a more useful comparison than the headline GPU-hour.

It won't hold everywhere. This is one provider's list price, capacity decides what you can actually get, and a compute-bound job may not benefit from the extra memory.
